bull.b: Strong Subsea inbound and a book-to-bill above one support forward revenue visibility and indicate demand is replenishing delivered work. The reiterated inbound target and record opportunity list also strengthen confidence that Subsea can remain the company’s durable growth engine.

The sharp improvement from earlier losses and near-breakeven periods demonstrates meaningful operating recovery across the business. Higher Subsea margins can support stronger earnings conversion and provide greater capacity to fund investment, returns, and execution through the cycle.

Robust cash generation combined with materially lower debt improves financial flexibility and reduces the balance-sheet burden carried in earlier years. This gives TechnipFMC more capacity to withstand project timing changes, support operations, and allocate capital while maintaining resilience.

bear.b: The recent turnaround has not eliminated the company’s exposure to offshore activity cycles. Earlier losses and uneven results show that earnings can weaken materially when customer investment slows, project activity softens, or execution conditions become less favorable.

Regional activity weakness and delayed final investment decisions can postpone conversion of backlog and opportunities into revenue. These timing issues may create uneven quarterly execution and keep parts of the business exposed to customer economics and local project conditions.

Competitive tendering can reduce pricing power and make future project awards less profitable than direct-award work. Although most work is direct-award, pressure on the tendered portion could constrain margin expansion and increase the importance of disciplined project selection.
